The University of Cincinnati's Center for Entrepreneurship is now providing financial support to CEAS students wishing to travel in order to compete in Hackathons.

The center will reimburse $0.625/mile traveled as per university recommendations.

# Travel Grant

Note: Travel funds for the Fall 2025 semester have been exhausted. We are currently accepting travel grant applications for the Spring 2026 semester.

The Virginia Tech Office of Undergraduate Research encourages students to present their research at conferences. OUR travel support program will cover expenses related to presenting at a conference. This rolling review process is designed to assist undergraduate students who have had their research or creative scholarship accepted for presentation at a regional, national or international conference. This program will provide travel funding to students who, without this support, may not be able to attend a conference to present their work. Current undergraduates from any discipline are eligible to apply for travel support.

The office will match funds you secure from other sources (such as your research mentor, department, college, student organization, student government, etc.) up to $750 for domestic travel and $1000 for international travel to support your travel, based on fund availability. Students must apply before they present at a conference. Please note that we are only able to fund one student per accepted presentation and students will only be eligible to receive travel support once per academic year. # The Office of Undergraduate Research and Major Awards

# Undergraduate Research Travel Fellowship
The Office of Undergraduate Research and Major Awards offers the Undergraduate Research
Travel Fellowship to support undergraduate students from the University of Houston
in enhancing their academic development, disseminating their research results, and
increasing the visibility of the institution by supporting undergraduate student travel
at regional, national, and international conferences. The travel funding is intended
for undergraduates presenting the results of their research or creative activities
at meetings for a regional, national, or international audience within their academic
discipline.
**The Undergraduate Research Travel Fellowship application is now closed for the 2024-2025
academic year. Please check back in August for the 2025-2026 URTF application.**
## Funding Offered
Students may apply for up to $500 to cover travel expenses associated with attending
and presenting their research or creative work at a conference.
The Undergraduate Research Travel Fellowship may not cover all expected travel expenses.
Students are strongly encouraged to seek additional funding through research grants,
conference travel award programs, and awards offered by their department

# Student Travel Grant

Call for Applications

Thanks to generous support from the National Science Foundation, we will provide a maximum of 15 scholarship awards to selected U.S.-based students attending the Florida Artificial Intelligence Research Society (FLAIRS) conference in Marco Island FL, May 17-20, 2026; see www.FLAIRS‑39.info. The scholarships will include financial support of $2500 for registration, travel, and lodging.

Expectations

Awardees must register for the conference and will have to make their own arrangements for travel and accommodation. Awardees must attend the conference in person, participate in pre- and post-surveys, participate daily in conference sessions, and attend a specially organized event for awardees only.

Eligibility

The objective of this award is to increase exposure to artificial intelligence activities and research for students who would otherwise not have this opportunity. Applicants must be full-time students (undergraduate or graduate) at a U.S.-based academic institution. Preference will be given to applicants who demonstrate a financial need that cannot be covered by their advisor or institution. The selection will be made based on the following criteria:

Computer Science (or related discipline) major,
